title: Richelieu to M. de Rancé, cipher letters of July 1629, BnF Français 3829 ff. 87 and 89

plaintext.source: Avenel, Lettres ... du cardinal de Richelieu, t. III (1858), nos. CXCIX (p. 368) and CCV (p. 381)

transcription.source: S. Tomokiyo, Unsolved Historical Ciphers (cryptiana); clear text only partly transcribed
transcription.notes: Counted by splitting richelieu1629.txt on ';' and keeping figure tokens (tilde forms counted separately); the --measure tool does not split semicolons. Ten transcription slips in Tomokiyo's text found, all confirmed by Avenel. Two letters under one key attacked as one.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution on two-digit figures 10-39 (19 letters scrambled plus two extra vowel sets), tilde for doubling, word codes and a nomenclature from 40.

diacritics.note: tilde over a figure doubles the letter (ll, nn, ss, ee)

system.notes: a has a fourth sign (39); 40 = de, 42 = la; ten nomenclature codes identified with Avenel's footnotes.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: 'la', 'd'autres', 'd'elle ... elle' (tilde = doubling), 'Brassac', 'l'ambassade' placed beside clear words.
Remaining letters from further words; alphabet and homophones recovered.
Avenel 1858 found to print both letters deciphered, with his reconstructed key.
Reading agrees with Avenel word for word; nomenclature codes resolved from his footnotes.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked the cryptiana transcription; saved the final.py decryption; copied the Avenel reading and the key table from SOLUTION.md to texts/

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): the two entries read: the raw decode of the partial transcription does not join into sentences (decoded, not read); Avenel's printed text reads (A, excerpt note added). Class already solved kept.

Re-reading (batch b33): DECODE R9461 and R9462 fetched with the project cookie: three colour scans, no attachment, transcription or comment; Avenel, Lettres de Richelieu III, pp. 367-386 fetched as Google Books page images (OIQItRIybmIC).
Avenel nos. CXCIX and CCV transcribed in full from the page images, with his printed figures and footnote decipherments (texts/ff87-89_avenel_figures.txt).

Every run of Avenel's printed figures decoded with the recovered key (research/reading_audit/b33_rl_decode.py): all agree with his footnotes; figure 39 corrected from a to et (both occurrences, 'frontiere et menee', 'Chevreuse et autres'); two figure slips (16 in 'menee au', final 29 in 'ambassada').

Three places checked on the manuscript scans: the clerk omitted the a of 'au' (Avenel's 16 is a misprint); f. 89v has 'a 51 30 18 52' (au roy et a la reyne mere), Avenel printed only 51; the second Brassac has the doubling stroke.

Running reading of both letters (texts/ff87-89_reading.md, English ff87-89_en.md): Avenel's clear text, ciphered words in the figures' spelling, codes named from his footnotes; body 0.826 clean sentences (b17 fr), 0.971 explicit holes only; entry 0 decoded, not read -> read (A).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The homophonic alphabet was rebuilt from Tomokiyo's transcription by placing cribs beside the clear words of the same letters ('la', 'd'autres', 'd'elle ... elle', 'Brassac' after 'Mr de', 'l'ambassade' after 'pour'); Avenel's 1858 decipherment (Lettres de Richelieu t. III) was found only after the reading and used to confirm it and to name ten nomenclator codes from his footnotes.
outcome.notes: Independent ciphertext-only recovery, later matched to Avenel's 1858 decipherment; Brassac's appointment to Rome in 1630 confirms. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the raw key decode was decoded, not read. 23 Oct 2026, re-reading: Avenel's text transcribed in full with his printed figures, every run decoded with the key and three places checked on the manuscript; both letters read (texts/ff87-89_reading.md). Class already solved kept.

texts.label: ff. 87 and 89 (7 and mid-July 1629), recovered key applied
texts.summary: Richelieu to M. de Rancé, July 1629: the King's anger at Bonneuil, a wish that the Duchesse de Chevreuse be seized near the frontier and taken to Vincennes, the cabals of Lorraine with Spain; and in mid-July the stalled peace with England, Henrietta Maria's French bishop and priests, and Brassac proposed for the Rome embassy.

reading_review.note: Both letters in full from Avenel 1858 (nos. CXCIX, CCV), transcribed from the page images with his printed figures; every run decoded with the recovered key gives his footnote decipherment; three places checked on the DECODE scans (Avenel's misprinted 16 in 'menée au', his omitted 'et 52' on f. 89v). Body 0.83 clean sentences (b17 fr), 0.97 explicit holes only; one hole.
